7	
8	# Attribute rubric
9	
10	Every test shipped with Maester declares what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques
11	it addresses. This page is the rule book for those values. Unit tests check what can be checked mechanically, and
12	a review step checks the judgement calls against this page. A custom test may use the same attributes; the rules
13	apply to it only if you want them to.
14	
15	The [test builder](/test-builder) lets you pick the values with this guidance beside each field and
16	shows the code as you go.
17	
18	| Question | Attributes | Required for built-in tests |
19	| --- | --- | --- |
20	| What is it about? | `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType` | All except `RelatedProduct` |
21	| What do I fix first? | `Severity`, `UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost` | `Severity` always. The other two unless `Severity` is `Info` |
22	| What does it map to? | `Mitre`, `Control` | `Mitre` (technique IDs or `None`) |
23	| Is it current? | `Lifecycle`, `ReplacedBy` | No. `Lifecycle` defaults to `Stable` |
24	
25	The allowed keys for `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` are in
26	[`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1).
27	Add a key there in the same pull request as the first test that needs it.
28	
29	## Rate the test, not your tenant
30	
31	Rate every value for a typical organization that fails the test, using the fix the test's own Markdown file
32	recommends. Do not rate for the best case, the worst case or one tenant you know. When two values fit, choose the
33	lower one for `Severity`, `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost`. A reader should be able to see the reason for
34	each value in the test's description and remediation text.
35	
36	## Product
37	
38	The product where the fix is made. One value.
39	
40	- Use the product whose admin surface holds the setting, not every product the test reads from.
41	- Tests in a product folder (`tests/maester/entra`, `tests/cisa/exchange`) use that folder's product.
42	- A product the test only reads from, or a licence it needs, is not a second product. `Service` and `License`
43	  already say that.
44	
45	## RelatedProduct
46	
47	Other products the test also checks or depends on. Optional list, never the same key as `Product`.
48	
49	- Add one when an admin of that product would expect to find the test under it. An Exchange Online test about an
50	  anti-phishing policy that is managed in the Defender portal has `RelatedProduct = 'defender'`.
51	- Add one when the fix is made in that product's portal although the test lives in another product's folder.
52	- Do not add a product only because its API is called.
53	
54	## Feature
55	
56	The part of the product the test is about. One key from the product's `Features` list.
57	
58	- Choose the feature whose settings page or object type the remediation sends the admin to.
59	- When a test spans two features, choose the one that fails most directly. A Conditional Access policy that
60	  requires a compliant device is `conditional-access`, not `devices`.
61	- Tests that check the same thing get the same feature, whatever folder or suite they are in.
62	- A feature that would hold one test only is usually too narrow. Prefer an existing feature.
63	
64	## Area
65	
66	The security theme, whatever the product. One key.
67	
68	| Key | Use it for |
69	| --- | --- |
70	| `authentication` | How an identity proves who it is: MFA, authentication methods, passwords, legacy protocols, Kerberos and NTLM hardening, session and token lifetime. |
71	| `privileged-access` | Administrative roles and accounts: who holds them, just-in-time elevation, emergency access, admin tiering, delegated admin rights. |
72	| `access-control` | Who may reach which resource under which conditions: device, location and risk conditions, permissions on objects, user defaults. |
73	| `applications` | App registrations, service principals and their credentials, consent and API permissions, OAuth apps, add-ins, connectors. |
74	| `external-access` | Guests, cross-tenant access, federation and trusts, external sharing and external communication. |
75	| `devices` | Device compliance, enrollment and configuration, endpoint protection, device identity. |
76	| `email-protection` | Anti-phishing, anti-spam and anti-malware, Safe Links and Safe Attachments, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, mail flow rules, meeting and messaging protections. |
77	| `data-protection` | Data loss prevention, sensitivity labels, encryption, retention, backup. |
78	| `logging-and-detection` | Audit logs, diagnostic settings, alert policies, sensors and the health of detection tooling. |
79	| `identity-lifecycle` | Stale and dormant accounts, ownership, access reviews, entitlement management, group membership hygiene. |
80	| `infrastructure` | The directory and platform itself: domain controllers, DNS, replication, sites, schema, Group Policy health, protocol hardening, subscriptions, tenant-wide platform settings. |
81	| `engineering-systems` | DevOps organizations, repositories, pipelines, build identities, the software supply chain. |
82	| `ai` | AI agents and copilots: who can use and share them, how they authenticate, what data and tools they reach. |
83	
84	When more than one area fits, choose by what the control is for, in this order:
85	
86	1. It protects administrators or admin rights: `privileged-access`.
87	2. It decides how sign-in is proven: `authentication`.
88	3. It is about an application, service principal or agent as the subject: `applications`, or `ai` for agents.
89	4. It is about people or data outside the organization: `external-access`.
90	5. Otherwise the area that names the mechanism: `access-control`, `devices`, `email-protection`,
91	   `data-protection`, `logging-and-detection`, `identity-lifecycle`, `engineering-systems`, `infrastructure`.
92	
93	A product never decides the area on its own. An Azure DevOps test about who is a Project Collection Administrator
94	is `privileged-access`, not `engineering-systems`.
95	
96	Inventory and health tests with no security theme of their own are `infrastructure`. When no area fits, choose
97	the closest and say so in the pull request, so the list can be reviewed.
98	
99	## ResourceType
100	
101	What a failing result points at. One key.
102	
103	- `Tenant` when the test evaluates one tenant-, organization-, forest- or domain-wide setting. The result is
104	  about the environment.
105	- `Tenant` when the test checks that at least one policy of a kind exists, even when it lists the policies that
106	  satisfy it. A failing result has nothing to list.
107	- `Tenant` when the test evaluates the single default or global policy of a kind, because there is one of it and
108	  it applies to everyone.
109	- Otherwise the kind of object a failing result lists or counts: `User`, `Application`, `Device`,
110	  `ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `GroupPolicy` and so on. A test that evaluates every policy and lists the ones that
111	  fail uses the policy type.
112	- A test that counts objects for review (an inventory test) uses the type it counts. When no key names that kind
113	  of object and it is a one-off, use `Tenant`.
114	- A family test, which yields one result per instance, uses the type of the instance.
115	
116	## Severity
117	
118	The risk to the organization while the test fails. Not the effort to fix it and not the disruption of fixing it.
119	
120	| Value | A failing result means |
121	| --- | --- |
122	| `Critical` | An attacker with no special position can take over the tenant, the domain or a privileged identity, or a secret is already exposed. Directly exploitable and wide in reach. |
123	| `High` | A primary control is missing or weakened for many users or for privileged identities, and common techniques such as phishing, password spray or consent phishing are enough to use it. |
124	| `Medium` | A defence-in-depth control is missing, or the exposure is limited to a few objects or one workload, or using it needs another weakness first. |
125	| `Low` | Hardening or hygiene with a small security effect on its own. |
126	| `Info` | The test reports a fact for review and makes no risk judgement. Info tests are left out of scores. |
127	
128	Decide in this order:
129	
130	1. **Reach.** Privileged identities or the whole tenant move the value up. A single workload or a few objects
131	   move it down.
132	2. **Directness.** Usable from the internet or by any signed-in user moves it up. Needing an earlier compromise
133	   moves it down. A password taken by phishing, spray or stuffing is not an earlier compromise: those are the
134	   common techniques `High` already assumes.
135	3. **Role of the control.** The main control for a threat rates higher than a second layer behind another control.
136	
137	`Critical` is rare. If the description cannot say in one sentence how an attacker gets from the failing state to
138	admin rights or exposed secrets, the value is `High` or lower. A benchmark's own wording does not set the value:
139	a SHALL policy can be `Medium`.
140	
141	Five cases come up often:
142	
143	- **A test that passes whenever its data can be read** is `Info`, whatever the data is about. If the fact
144	  deserves a severity, the test should fail on it.
145	- **A failure that is only an outage or untidiness**, such as replication health, an expiring token or an unused
146	  object, is `Low`. It is `Medium` or higher only when the outage switches off a security control, and then it is
147	  rated as the loss of that control.
148	- **Alerts and notifications** are a second layer behind the control they watch, so they are `Medium` at most.
149	- **The same check in two suites** gets the same value in both. Usually the second is a shim that returns the
150	  first test's result and declares all of its values; see
151	  [Tests that another suite already has](./index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).
152	- **The main control against an attack that starts from a stolen password** is `High`. A second layer behind
153	  that control is `Medium`. Number matching against MFA fatigue is `High`; showing the app name and location in
154	  the prompt is `Medium`.
155	
156	Anchors from existing tests:
157	
158	| Test | Value | Why |
159	| --- | --- | --- |
160	| No Group Policy object contains a `cpassword` | `Critical` | Any domain user can read and decrypt the stored password. |
161	| No domain admin account has a service principal name | `Critical` | Any domain user can request a ticket and crack an admin password offline. |
162	| Legacy authentication is blocked | `High` | Password spray bypasses MFA for every user. |
163	| Number matching is required for Authenticator push notifications | `High` | MFA fatigue works against any user once a password is phished. |
164	| Authenticator shows the app name and location | `Medium` | A second layer behind number matching. |
165	| Users cannot register applications | `Medium` | Needs a signed-in user and a further step to cause harm. |
166	| MailTips are enabled for end users | `Low` | A small aid against mis-sent mail. |
167	| Disabled user count should be retrievable | `Info` | Inventory for review. |
168	| [EIDSCA.AP14 — users may read other users](/docs/tests/EIDSCA.AP14) | `Info` | Disabling `allowedToReadOtherUsers` is not itself a security finding. Review the restriction because it can disrupt collaboration, user lookup and default features. |
169	
170	Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment) rates many of the same
171	Microsoft Entra and Intune settings. Where it has a test for the same setting, compare your value with its risk
172	level and give the reason in the pull request if the two differ.
173	
174	## UserImpact
175	
176	How much the recommended fix disrupts end users. Administrators and the owners of applications are not end
177	users here. Developers are the end users of Azure DevOps and GitHub.
178	
179	| Value | Applying the fix |
180	| --- | --- |
181	| `Low` | End users notice nothing, or only administrators are affected. |
182	| `Medium` | Some users change how they work or meet a new prompt: a group loses a capability, users register a method once, a legacy client stops working for a subset. |
183	| `High` | Most users change a daily habit, or a mistake locks people out or stops mail or an app for many. Needs communication and a staged rollout. |
184	
185	Omit `UserImpact` when `Severity` is `Info`.
186	
187	## ImplementationCost
188	
189	How much administrator work the recommended fix takes.
190	
191	| Value | The fix is |
192	| --- | --- |
193	| `Low` | One setting or one policy in one portal. Under an hour, with no dependency on another team, a licence purchase or a rollout. |
194	| `Medium` | Several steps: a policy that needs exclusions and a pilot, clean-up of a handful of objects, coordination with one other team. Hours to a few days. |
195	| `High` | A project: new licences, infrastructure or process, a migration of users or apps, or clean-up across many objects. Weeks or more. |
196	
197	Clean-up that one administrator can finish alone in a sitting is `Low`. Clean-up that needs the owner of each
198	object is `Medium`. Turning on a plan that is billed by use is `Medium`: the click is easy, the budget approval is
199	not. Count the work of the fix, including exclusions and rollout, but not the time to decide.
200	
201	Omit `ImplementationCost` when `Severity` is `Info`.
202	
203	## Mitre
204	
205	The MITRE ATT&CK techniques that the checked control prevents or detects. A list of technique IDs, or `None`.
206	
207	- IDs only, in the form `T1110` or `T1110.003`. Tactic names are looked up from the pinned ATT&CK release
208	  (`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`) and are never typed.
209	- Use a sub-technique when the control addresses only that sub-technique. When three or more sub-techniques of
210	  one technique apply, list the technique instead. Do not list a technique together with one of its own
211	  sub-techniques.
212	- List a technique only if the test's description explains, or plainly implies, how the control stops or reveals
213	  it. At most five.
214	- A test that implements a benchmark which publishes a mapping, such as CISA SCuBA, starts from that mapping and
215	  then applies these rules. An ID the pinned release has retired is replaced by its successor in that release,
216	  found by name.
217	- The description means the comment-based help and the Markdown file together.
218	- Use `None` for a test with no attacker behaviour behind it, such as replication health or an inventory count.
219	  An inventory test lists a technique only when the fact it reports is itself the precondition of that technique,
220	  such as accounts that do not require Kerberos pre-authentication.
221	- A retired or unknown ID fails the unit tests.
222	
223	## Control
224	
225	Requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports, written `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`, for
226	example `cis-m365:5.1.5.1`, `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` or `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)`. Optional list. Any test can use
227	it: one shipped with Maester or one of your own.
228	
229	- `Control` is the only way a test is mapped to a framework. A CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'` and
230	  a CISA test carries `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` and an ASD test `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`.
231	  Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its suite's framework. The unit
232	  tests check this.
233	- The first value that names a requirement in a framework file becomes the `Benchmark` of the result. Put the
234	  requirement the test is written for first, and any other requirement it supports after it.
235	- Use the same attribute for a test that exists for its own reasons and also supports a requirement: a Maester
236	  test that checks the setting a CISA policy asks for, or a CIS test that also supports a NIST control.
237	- When the key is a framework shipped with Maester (`cis-m365`, `cis-github`, `cisa-scuba`, `essential-eight`, `ism`), the requirement must
238	  exist in that framework's file. If it is new, add it to the file with its facts. The module build and the unit
239	  tests fail otherwise.
240	- Do not repeat the `Related` controls of a requirement. The framework file lists them and Maester adds them to
241	  the result.
242	- List a requirement only when a passing result is evidence for it. A test that checks one part of a requirement
243	  may list it; a test that is merely on the same topic may not.
244	
245	A reference says the test supports the requirement. It never says the organization complies with it.
246	
247	### NIST SP 800-53
248	
249	A test may list the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls its setting implements, as `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`.
250	
251	- Use an ID from the pinned list, [`powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json):
252	  a base control (`AC-2`) or an enhancement (`IA-2(1)`). The unit tests reject anything else.
253	- List a control only when a passing result is direct evidence that it is implemented for what the test checks.
254	- Prefer the enhancement when the test checks exactly what it says: MFA for privileged accounts is `IA-2(1)`.
255	  Do not list a base control together with one of its own enhancements.
256	- At most three, best fit first. Never the policy-and-procedures controls (`AC-1`, `IA-1` and so on).
257	- A test that only reports a count, or checks health, licensing or tidiness, lists none, unless the count is
258	  itself what a control asks to be tracked: dormant accounts for `AC-2(3)`.
259	- A test that implements a CISA SCuBA policy does not list NIST controls. CISA publishes that mapping, the

    .SYNOPSIS

    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CIS.M365.5.2.3.4',
        Title = 'Ensure all member users are ''MFA capable''',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'authentication-methods',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'User',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',

        Author = 'JeremyFinney-lgtm'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    Write-Verbose 'Getting the user registration details report...'
    $filter = 'isMfaCapable eq false'
    $registrations = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails' -Filter $filter
    $notCapable = @($registrations | Where-Object { $_.userType -eq 'Member' -and $_.userDisplayName -notmatch 'On-Premises Directory Synchronization Service Account' })
    $testResult = $notCapable.Count -eq 0

    $passText = 'All member users are registered for a method that can satisfy multifactor authentication.'
    $failText = "$($notCapable.Count) member user(s) are not MFA capable."

    $resultMd = "| User | Administrator | Result |`n"
    $resultMd += "| --- | --- | --- |`n"
    foreach ($user in ($notCapable | Sort-Object -Property isAdmin, userPrincipalName -Descending | Select-Object -First 50)) {
        $resultMd += "| $($user.userPrincipalName) | $($user.isAdmin) | ❌ Fail |`n"
    }
    if ($notCapable.Count -gt 50) {
        $resultMd += "`nShowing 50 of $($notCapable.Count) users."
    }
    if ($testResult) {

﻿Every member user has registered at least one authentication method that can satisfy multifactor authentication.

A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA only helps if users can complete it. A user who has not registered a usable method is either locked out when the policy is enforced or is excluded from it, and in both cases the account is protected by a password alone.

The test reads the registration report, which can lag behind recent changes by a short time. Accounts that are not used for interactive sign-in should be reviewed and, if no longer needed, disabled or removed.

5. Disable or delete accounts that are no longer in use.

# userRegistrationDetails resource type - Microsoft Graph v1.0 | Microsoft Learn

Namespace: microsoft.graph

Represents the state of a user's authentication methods, including which methods are registered and which features the user is registered and capable of, such as multifactor authentication, self-service password reset, and passwordless authentication. For more information about license requirements for this feature, see [Authentication Methods Activity: Permissions and licenses](/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-authentication-methods-activity#permissions-and-licenses).

Inherits from [entity](entity).

## Methods

| Method | Return type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [List](../authenticationmethodsroot-list-userregistrationdetails) | [userRegistrationDetails](userregistrationdetails) collection | Get a list of the authentication methods registered for a user as defined in the [userRegistrationDetails](userregistrationdetails) object. |
| [Get](../userregistrationdetails-get) | [userRegistrationDetails](userregistrationdetails) | Read the properties and relationships of a [userRegistrationDetails](userregistrationdetails) object. |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | String | User object identifier in Microsoft Entra ID. Inherited from [entity](entity). |
| isAdmin | Boolean | Indicates whether the user has an [admin role](/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference?toc=%2Fgraph%2Ftoc.json) in the tenant. This value can be used to check the authentication methods that privileged accounts are registered for and capable of. |
| isMfaCapable | Boolean | Indicates whether the user has registered a strong authentication method for multifactor authentication. The method must be allowed by the [authentication methods policy](authenticationmethodspolicy). Supports `$filter` (`eq`). |
| isMfaRegistered | Boolean | Indicates whether the user has registered a strong authentication method for multifactor authentication. The method may not necessarily be allowed by the [authentication methods policy](authenticationmethodspolicy). Supports `$filter` (`eq`). |

# device resource type - Microsoft Graph v1.0 | Microsoft Learn

Namespace: microsoft.graph

Represents a device registered in the organization. Devices are created in the cloud using the Device Registration Service or by Intune. They're used by conditional access policies for multi-factor authentication. These devices can range from desktop and laptop machines to phones and tablets. Inherits from [directoryObject](directoryobject).

This resource is an open type that allows additional properties beyond those documented here.

This resource supports:

- Adding your own data to custom properties as [extensions](/en-us/graph/extensibility-overview).
- Using [delta query](/en-us/graph/delta-query-overview) to track incremental additions, deletions, and updates, by providing a [delta](../user-delta) function.
- [OData query capabilities](/en-us/graph/query-parameters) including `$select`, `$filter`, `$search`, and `$top`. Specific usages are supported only with [Advanced query capabilities](/en-us/graph/aad-advanced-queries#group-properties).

## Facts about the mirrors that differ from the brief or design

- The mirrors commit once per crawl run, not once per page. A run lists its pages in the commit message.
- Runs after a Learn metadata change rewrite the front matter of thousands of pages (intune 2026-10-29 "3054
  changed" and 2026-11-04 "3567 changed"; entra 2026-10-29 "3836 changed"). Test-MtStepSource therefore compares
  page bodies and ignores front-matter-only commits. Without that, every source would show as changed after each
  such crawl.
- `.learn-mirror/state.json` maps every en-us page URL to its file (`path`), with `redirectedTo` and `aliasOf`
  entries. The index is built from it (16,728 pages over nine mirrors), falling back to front-matter canonicalUrl.
- Learn's HEAD answers are unreliable for redirects: HEAD returned 200 for
  microsoft-365/security/defender/microsoft-secure-score (GET: 301 to defender-xdr/...), and plain and Markdown HEAD
  disagree on mem/intune and intune/intune-service URLs. The resolver sends GET, reads headers only, Accept
  text/markdown, one hop at a time, 4 requests a second, cached 30 days.

- **Scope.** A step is in scope when a row that ran names it, or when it is a prerequisite, at any depth, of
  such a step. A goal is in scope when any of its steps is. A row ran when its result is anything but
  `NotRun`.
- **Tests come from the inventory, not only the rows.** `Tests` lists every test the engine knows that names
  the step: built-in tests from the catalog, custom tests that were discovered, and pack tests from each pack's
  catalogue. A test with no row has `Result` `NotRun` and `ReasonCode` `NotInRun`. The report can then name the
  command that checks it. This is how `Frameworks` already lists requirements that no row checks.
- **`Measure`** is set on a step that has one, whether or not it could be read:
  `{ "Key": "devices-compliant", "Count": 412, "Total": 580, "Share": 71, "MinimumShare": 95, "Met": false,
  "ReadAt": "...", "ObjectCount": 168, "Objects": [{ "Type": "Device", "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }],
  "ReasonCode": null }`. `Objects` holds up to 100 of the objects that fall short. `ReasonCode` says why a measure
  couldn't be read, with the same codes a skipped test uses.
- **`Earlier`** is set on a step that is Not checked in this run when an earlier result in the output folder
  checked it: `{ "Status": "Done", "ExecutedAt": "...", "File": "..." }`. It is never mixed into this run's
  status or counts. `Get-MtPreviousResult` gains `LastKnown`, which is the newest earlier result for each test ID
  a step in scope names. It reads only files that `History` already lists, and only when some step in scope is
  Not checked. Today `Results` covers the newest earlier run only, and after a one-check run that run says
  little.
- **Goal status** is `Done` when every applicable step is Done, `NotStarted` when none is, and `InProgress`
  otherwise. When a step is Unknown or Not checked, the goal shows that count next to its progress.

## 11. Measures

Seven steps in the first catalogue have no check. Two of them are tenant states that a figure from Graph
settles, so in Phase 1 they get measures, not tests. The owner ruled on 5 November 2026 that readiness is a data
point, not a test. A share of compliant devices isn't a misconfiguration and has no meaningful severity or
ATT&CK technique, so it must not change pass rates or the test count. A measure also runs whenever its step is
in scope, so "Before you fix this" shows a real figure even after a one-test run, where a test would have had
to be selected.

A measure is an entry in the measure registry, `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`:

```powershell
@{
    Measures = @(
        @{
            Key         = 'devices-compliant'
            Function    = 'Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare'
            Title       = 'Devices that sign in are compliant'
            Unit        = 'devices'
            Service     = 'Graph'
            License     = 'INTUNE_A'
            Permission  = 'Graph:Scope:Device.Read.All'
        }
    )
}
```

- `Service`, `License` and `Permission` use the grammar of the test attributes, and the engine applies them the
  way it gates a test. A measure whose gate fails is Unknown with the matching reason code.
- `Function` names an internal reader in `powershell/internal/services/<service>/`. It reads through the Graph
  cache and returns `Count` (the objects that meet the bar), `Total`, and `Objects` (those that fall short, as
  `Type`, `Id` and `DisplayName`). The engine keeps up to 100 of them.
- The engine works out `Share`, compares it with the step's `MinimumShare` or the run config's override, and
  writes the result to the step (section 7.2).
- Readers write object facts with the shared keys (section 12) for the objects they list.

| Key | Step | Reads | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `devices-compliant` | `intune.devices-compliant` | Entra `devices` that signed in within 30 days, by `isManaged` and `isCompliant` | The objects are the devices a compliant-device policy would block. Devices with no Entra identity can't be seen, and the result says so |
| `mfa-registered` | `entra.mfa-registered` | `reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` for enabled member users | Needs Entra ID P1. Leaves out the emergency access accounts |

Later: phishing-resistant method registration for all users (ZTA.21782 covers privileged users only),
password writeback once a Graph API reports it, security defaults being off in tenants licensed for
Conditional Access (section 15), and hybrid join and Windows device registration, which need sign-in data to
see the devices that have no identity yet. The Defender–Intune connector is partly covered already.
MT.1098 checks that Mobile Threat Defense connectors are healthy. Whether it fails when the Defender connector
is missing is confirmed in the expert pass.

A measure isn't a test: it has no ID, no row in `Tests` and no attribute review, and it plays no part in pass
rates, frameworks or the test count. Packs can't add measures in Phase 1.

## 12. Object facts

The Zero Trust facts work (`Add-MtAffectedObjectFact`, maester365/maester#2681) puts facts on
listed objects: join type, managed and compliant for devices, MFA and passwordless for users. They are the
drill-down behind a lane ("38 devices aren't managed"). They can't replace measures, because facts attach
only to objects the run lists and come from the Zero Trust export only when it ran. Measures write facts too.

This design asked that work to give each fact a stable key and a raw value before the command ships, so that a
lane's drill-down never parses display text. It did, in maester365/maester#2681: a fact has `Name`, `Value`
(display text), `Tone`, an optional `Key` (dotted camelCase, `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\.[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)+$`), an
optional `Raw` (boolean, number, string, string list, or ISO 8601 UTC date), `Source` and `AsOf`. A fact with the
same `Key` from the same `Source` replaces the earlier one. The shared keys are listed under "Fact keys" in
`website/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results.md`. The ones this design reads:

| Key | Raw | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device.managed`, `device.compliant` | bool | The devices behind `intune.devices-compliant`. Management and compliance are separate facts |
| `device.joinType` | `AzureAd`, `ServerAd` or `Workplace` | Join coverage, for hybrid join and token protection |
| `device.os` | string | Which platforms need a compliance policy |
| `user.mfaRegistered`, `user.passwordless` | bool | The users behind `entra.mfa-registered` and the phishing-resistant steps |
| `user.privilegedRoles` | string list | The admins step of phishing-resistant MFA, and the privileged access goal |
| `signIn.daysSince` | int, or null when none is recorded | Leaving out stale devices and users. Counted from the fact's `AsOf`, not from now |

User facts are recorded under both the object ID and the UPN, so a record has them whichever way it was keyed.
The measures write the same keys for the objects they list.

The sources are the nine Learn mirrors built with `merill/learn-mirror`. They crawl Learn four times a day and
make one commit per changed page. They cover Entra, Intune, Defender, security (Zero Trust), Purview, Teams,

function Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the devices that signed in recently and are marked compliant, for the devices-compliant measure.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The reader of the devices-compliant measure (powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1), which decides the step
    intune.devices-compliant of the defender's path. A Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device
    blocks every device that Microsoft Entra ID doesn't mark compliant, so the share of compliant devices among the
    devices in use says whether such a policy can be turned on.

    Reads the enabled devices in Microsoft Entra ID that signed in within the last SignedInWithinDays days
    (approximateLastSignInDateTime), through the Graph cache. A device counts when isCompliant is true: Intune or
    an approved MDM sets it, and it is what a compliant-device grant checks. Devices that are not compliant are
    returned as the objects that fall short, most recent sign-in first, whether they are managed (isManaged) and
    noncompliant or not managed at all.

    A device that has no Microsoft Entra identity (neither registered nor joined) can't be seen this way, so it is
    neither counted nor listed. A compliant-device policy blocks it too.

    Returns an object with Count (compliant devices), Total (devices that signed in) and Objects (the devices that
    aren't compliant, as Type, Id and DisplayName).

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare

    Returns the number of compliant devices among the enabled devices that signed in within the last 30 days.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare -SignedInWithinDays 14

        Total   = $devices.Count
        Objects = @(

                Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { [string]$_.approximateLastSignInDateTime }; Descending = $true }, displayName, id |

                        Type        = 'Device'
                        Id          = [string]$_.id

    }

- `powershell/internal/services/entra/Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare.ps1`: reads `devices` with

  users, `Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount` users and the user members of its groups (recursive), and user members of
  the DirectorySynchronizationAccounts / OnPremisesDirectorySyncAccount roles. Objects = unregistered users,
  admins first.
- `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`: entries `devices-compliant` (no License, see below) and
  `mfa-registered` (License AAD_PREMIUM, AuditLog.Read.All).
- `powershell/tests/functions/MeasureReaders.Tests.ps1`.

## For whoever merges M2 and M5

Steps files were not touched. Add to the catalogue, and delete each step's `Unchecked` line:

- `intune.devices-compliant`: `"Measure": { "Key": "devices-compliant", "MinimumShare": 95 }`
- `entra.mfa-registered`: `"Measure": { "Key": "mfa-registered", "MinimumShare": 95 }`

## Open points for the design owner

- The design's registry example gives `devices-compliant` `License = 'INTUNE_A'`. Left out: an approved
